images.title: Ladder recap: HCF and LCM
images.purpose: Recap how one ladder gives both the HCF from the divisors and the LCM from the divisors and the last row.
images.composition: A small one step ladder in the centre left with two coloured arrows to two result lines on the right, lots of white space.
exact_structure: Ladder rows: 36 and 48, then 3 and 4. Exactly 2 rows, 4 numbers.
Exactly 1 divisor, 12, in a teal #0072B2 circle to the left of row 1, with grey #6B7280 division bars.
The bottom row 3 and 4 is in amber #E69F00, with the small grey note co-prime, stop beside it.
One teal arrow from the divisor 12 to the line HCF = 12.
One reddish purple #CC79A7 arrow from the divisor and the bottom row together to the line LCM = 12 × 3 × 4 = 144.
rejection: a bottom row other than 3 and 4, an HCF other than 12 or an LCM other than 144
a second divisor or a third ladder row
images.takeaway: Stop when the last row is co-prime: the divisors give the HCF, and the divisors times the last row give the LCM.
images.description: A ladder dividing 36 and 48 by 12 to get 3 and 4, with arrows to HCF = 12 and LCM = 12 × 3 × 4 = 144.
images.context: Shown beside the practice on climbing the division ladder.
images.teaching_notes: For each practice pair, stop at a co-prime row, then follow the teal arrow for the HCF and the purple one for the LCM.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap of both readings of the ladder supports the practice tool.
